records.title: Structured video debriefing with a coach and laparoscopic skill scores in general surgery residents over one academic year
records.authors: Ferrante-Osei L, Kowalczyk-Adams M, Nwachukwu-Berg T
records.abstract: We followed 36 general surgery residents in two programmes through one academic year. Twenty residents chose to take part in monthly video debriefing of a filmed laparoscopic cholecystectomy with a trained consultant coach; 16 did not. Two blinded raters scored one video per resident at the start and end of the year with a five-domain global rating scale (score 5 to 25). Scores rose by a mean of 4.1 points in coached residents and 2.3 points in residents who were not coached, a difference of 1.8 points (95 percent CI 0.4 to 3.2) after adjustment for training year. Residents who chose coaching had higher baseline scores, and self-selection may explain part of the difference.

records.title: Reliability of blinded video rating of laparoscopic cholecystectomy with a global rating scale
records.abstract: Operative skill is often judged by the supervising surgeon, who knows the trainee. We asked three surgeons who did not know the trainees to rate 60 edited videos of laparoscopic cholecystectomy with a five-domain global rating scale. Inter-rater reliability was good (intraclass correlation 0.79 for the total score), and two raters were enough for decisions about change over time. Rating one video took about 12 minutes once the video had been edited to the critical steps. Reliability was lower for the domain on flow of the operation. Unedited full-length videos took three times as long to rate without improving agreement.

records.title: Peer versus consultant video coaching for surgical trainees: a randomised comparison
records.authors: Adeyemi-Sato K, Brennan-Iqbal R, Holm-Mensah D
records.abstract: Forty-eight residents were randomly allocated to video coaching by a senior peer or by a consultant for six months, with one coaching session a month. Both groups improved on blinded global rating scale scores, by 3.6 points with peer coaching and 3.9 points with consultant coaching, a difference within the pre-specified margin of 1.5 points. Consultant sessions lasted a mean of 45 minutes and peer sessions 35 minutes. There was no group without coaching, so the study cannot show whether coaching itself improves skill. Loss to follow-up was 10 percent, mostly residents who changed rotation.

records.title: Residents' views on filming their operations for coaching and assessment in three training programmes
records.abstract: We asked 112 surgical residents in three programmes about filming and reviewing their operations; 81 responded. Most (72 percent) were willing to have operations filmed for coaching, but only 38 percent were willing for the same videos to be used in formal assessment. Residents worried about who could see the videos and how long they were kept. Female residents and junior residents were more likely to worry that videos would be used against them. Willingness was higher when the resident could choose which cases to film and when videos were deleted after review.

records.title: Video coaching and intraoperative autonomy ratings in junior surgical residents
records.venue: Proceedings of the Surgical Training Forum
records.abstract: Junior residents who received three video coaching sessions were compared with junior residents in the same programme who did not. Attending surgeons rated intraoperative autonomy on a four-level scale after each operation. Coached residents reached the level of performing the operation with passive help earlier, after a median of 14 operations against 19 operations for residents who were not coached. Raters were not blinded to coaching, the number of residents is not reported in the abstract, and the conference listing gives no year of presentation.

response.synthesis: Five retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. One prospective comparison found that residents who chose video debriefing gained 1.8 more points on a blinded rating scale over a year, but self-selection may explain part of this. A randomised comparison showed peer and consultant coaching work similarly, without an uncoached group. Blinded rating of edited videos is reliable with two raters. Residents accept filming for coaching far more than for assessment. The evidence supports measuring coaching locally but gives only a rough effect size.
response.gradeRationale: One small non-randomised comparison, one randomised study without an uncoached group, and indirect or unblinded evidence; direction consistent, serious risk of bias and imprecision.
response.summary: Five retrieved records appraised; three claims recorded; overall certainty low.

response.reading: Coaching sits between filming, which already happens, and skill, which nobody measures. The retrieved evidence gives a way to measure skill (blinded rating of edited videos) and a rough size of change, but warns that residents who choose coaching differ from those who do not. Trust decides participation: residents accept filming for coaching, not for assessment.

response.overview: Prospective observational comparison of residents who take part in monthly video review coaching and residents who do not, over the 2027 to 2028 academic year in one general surgery programme.
response.population: All 14 general surgery residents in the programme in July 2027; residents who leave the programme are followed until they leave.
response.exposure: Monthly video review coaching: the resident and a consultant coach review a filmed laparoscopic cholecystectomy or appendicectomy for about 45 minutes. Participation is voluntary and recorded at each session.
response.procedures: Each resident films one laparoscopic cholecystectomy in July to September 2027 and one in April to June 2028. Videos are edited to the critical steps and rated independently by two consultants who do not coach that resident, blind to coaching status and to timing. response.sampleSize: The sample is fixed at the 14 residents in the programme. If about 8 take part in coaching and 6 do not, and the standard deviation of change is about 2 points (retrieved comparison), the 95 percent confidence interval for the difference in change will be roughly 2.3 points either side of the estimate, too wide to exclude no effect if the true difference is 1.8 points. The study is therefore reported as a local estimate with its interval, and as a source of variance estimates for a multi-programme study.

response.title: Video review coaching and change in blinded operative skill scores among general surgery residents: a prospective observational study
response.abstract: Objective: to estimate whether residents who take part in monthly video review coaching gain more operative skill over one academic year than residents who do not. Design: prospective observational comparison in one general surgery programme. Participants: the 14 residents of the 2027 to 2028 academic year. Outcome: change in a blinded global rating scale score for laparoscopic cholecystectomy, adjusted for baseline score and training year. Results will be reported when rating is complete.
response.introduction: Video review coaching is spreading in surgical training because filming is now easy. Most published comparisons contrast one form of coaching with another or rely on unblinded ratings by supervisors. This study measures skill change blind to coaching status in a programme where coaching is voluntary.
response.methods: Every resident films one laparoscopic cholecystectomy at the start and one at the end of the year. Videos are edited to the critical steps and scored by two consultants who do not coach that resident, blind to coaching status and timing. Change in score is compared between coached and uncoached residents by linear regression adjusted for baseline score and training year. Study videos are kept out of assessment and deleted after rating.
response.results: No videos have been rated yet. The report will give the adjusted difference in change with its confidence interval, autonomy ratings and coaching attendance.
response.discussion: The estimate will be imprecise with 14 residents and will be presented as a local result and a source of planning values for a multi-programme study. Self-selection into coaching will be discussed as the main alternative explanation.
response.limitations: Small sample, self-selection into coaching, one programme and one index operation. Autonomy ratings are not blinded.
response.conclusion: To be written after rating. It will not claim an effect on patient outcomes.
